description: Curated narrator biography (rijal) knowledge base for the Hadith Research Agent.
provenance: Facts (name, generation, death year, reliability) are drawn from standard classical rijāl references — Ibn Hajar al-Asqalani's Taqrib al-Tahdhib, al-Dhahabi's Siyar A'lam al-Nubala' and Mizan al-I'tidal — and are advisory. This is a curated starter subset (famous Companions, prominent Successors, and the compilers of the major collections) for offline, deterministic use; it is not an exhaustive rijāl dictionary. Where classical critics disagree, the note says so and the headline reliability is the more cautious reading.

reliabilities.thiqa: Trustworthy — relied upon as an authoritative narrator
reliabilities.saduq: Truthful — accepted with corroboration or in less demanding contexts
reliabilities.daif: Weak — not relied upon for primary evidence
reliabilities.matruk: Abandoned — rejected as a hadith narrator by the critics

narrators.name: Abu Bakr al-Siddiq
narrators.note: First Rightly-Guided Caliph and the closest Companion of the Prophet (peace be upon him).

narrators.name: Umar ibn al-Khattab
narrators.note: Second Rightly-Guided Caliph; narrator of the hadith of intentions (opening hadith of Sahih al-Bukhari).

narrators.name: Uthman ibn Affan
narrators.note: Third Rightly-Guided Caliph; oversaw the standardized compilation of the Qur'anic text.

narrators.name: Ali ibn Abi Talib
narrators.note: Fourth Rightly-Guided Caliph, cousin and son-in-law of the Prophet.

narrators.name: Abdullah ibn Abbas
narrators.note: Cousin of the Prophet, called 'the scholar of the Ummah'; foremost authority on tafsir among the Companions.

narrators.name: Abdullah ibn Umar
narrators.note: Son of Umar; a careful and prolific narrator of hadith.

narrators.name: Abdullah ibn Mas'ud
narrators.note: Early Companion, authority on Qur'an and fiqh; large number of narrations.

narrators.name: Abdullah ibn Amr ibn al-As
narrators.note: Companion who wrote down hadith with the Prophet's permission (as-sahifah as-sadiqah).

narrators.name: Abu Hurayrah
narrators.note: Companion who narrated the largest number of hadith.

narrators.name: Anas ibn Malik
narrators.note: Companion who served the Prophet as a youth and narrated widely.

narrators.name: Aishah bint Abi Bakr
narrators.note: Wife of the Prophet and a major narrator; the scholars of the Ummah deferred to her on many rulings.

narrators.name: Jabir ibn Abdullah
narrators.note: Companion of the Ansar; among the most prolific narrators.

narrators.name: Abu Sa'id al-Khudri
narrators.note: Companion of the Ansar and frequent narrator of legal hadith.

narrators.name: Abu Musa al-Ash'ari
narrators.note: Companion, governor, and one of the four caliphs' envoys for the standardized Qur'an.

narrators.name: Mu'adh ibn Jabal
narrators.note: Companion famed for knowledge of halal and haram; died young in the plague of 'Amwas.

narrators.name: Zayd ibn Thabit
narrators.note: Chief scribe of the revelation; compiled the Qur'an under Abu Bakr.

narrators.name: Ubayy ibn Ka'b
narrators.note: Reciter and foremost authority on the Qur'an among the Companions; death year given variously as 19-30 AH.

narrators.name: Salman al-Farisi
narrators.note: Companion from Persia; the Prophet said of him, 'Salman is from us, the People of the House.'

narrators.name: Bilal ibn Rabah
narrators.note: First mu'adhdhin of Islam.

narrators.name: Abu Dharr al-Ghifari
narrators.note: Companion known for asceticism and candor.

narrators.name: Abu Ayyub al-Ansari
narrators.note: Companion whose home hosted the Prophet upon arrival in Madinah.

narrators.name: Al-Nu'man ibn Bashir
narrators.note: Companion and later governor; narrator of the 'lawful is clear and the unlawful is clear' hadith.

narrators.name: Umm Salama
narrators.note: Wife of the Prophet; narrations recorded through her.

narrators.name: Hafsa bint Umar
narrators.note: Wife of the Prophet; keeper of the manuscript used for the standardized Qur'an.

narrators.name: Imran ibn Husayn
narrators.note: Companion; the Prophet prayed for his forgiveness.

narrators.name: Sa'id ibn al-Musayyab
narrators.note: Foremost of the Seven Fuqaha of Madinah; considered the most learned Successor.

narrators.name: Ibn Shihab al-Zuhri
narrators.note: Pioneer of hadith compilation; relied upon by every major collection.

narrators.name: Mujahid ibn Jabr
narrators.note: Student of Ibn Abbas and a leading authority on tafsir.

narrators.name: Qatadah ibn Di'amah
narrators.note: Blind scholar of Basra, celebrated for memory and exegesis.

narrators.name: Al-Hasan al-Basri
narrators.note: Famous Successor, ascetic and preacher of Basra.

narrators.name: Muhammad ibn Sirin
narrators.note: Successor of Basra, authority on hadith and dream interpretation.

narrators.name: Ata ibn Abi Rabah
narrators.note: Makkah's mufti and a leading Successor.

narrators.name: Nafi' (mawla of Ibn Umar)
narrators.note: Freed slave and long-time companion of Ibn Umar; the Maliki school's preferred chain runs through him.

narrators.name: Urwa ibn al-Zubayr
narrators.note: Son of al-Zubayr and Asma', nephew of Aishah; a leading Madinan jurist.

narrators.name: Abu Salama ibn Abd al-Rahman
narrators.note: Madinan Successor and a major narrator from Abu Hurayrah and Aishah.

narrators.name: Salim ibn Abdullah ibn Umar
narrators.note: Grandson of Umar; praised by Malik as among the most authentic of Ibn Umar's transmitters.

narrators.name: Alqamah ibn Waqqas
narrators.note: Successor; key link in the chain of the intentions hadith.

narrators.name: Sa'id ibn Jubayr
narrators.note: Student of Ibn Abbas; executed by al-Hajjaj. Trustworthy.

narrators.name: Ikrimah (mawla of Ibn Abbas)
narrators.note: Freed slave and student of Ibn Abbas; disputed by some critics but accepted by most.

narrators.name: Abu Wa'il (Shaqiq ibn Salama)
narrators.note: Kufan Successor; narrator from Ibn Mas'ud and Ali.

narrators.name: Malik ibn Anas
narrators.note: Imam of Madinah and author of the Muwatta; the scholars are unanimous on his trustworthiness.

narrators.name: Sufyan al-Thawri
narrators.note: Kufan imam; one of the most rigorous hadith critics of his generation.

narrators.name: Shu'ba ibn al-Hajjaj
narrators.note: Called 'commander of the faithful in hadith' by Ahmad; pioneering isnad critic.

narrators.name: Yahya ibn Sa'id al-Qattan
narrators.note: Basran imam and leading critic of narrators.

narrators.name: Ahmad ibn Hanbal
narrators.note: Imam of the Hanbali school and author of the Musnad.

narrators.name: Muhammad ibn Isma'il al-Bukhari
narrators.note: Compiler of the Sahih; the most celebrated hadith critic.

narrators.name: Muslim ibn al-Hajjaj
narrators.note: Compiler of the Sahih; student of al-Bukhari.

narrators.name: Abu Dawud al-Sijistani
narrators.note: Compiler of the Sunan; collected 4,800 hadith of fiqh from 500,000.

narrators.name: Muhammad ibn Isa al-Tirmidhi
narrators.note: Compiler of the Jami'; pioneered the systematic grading of hadith.

narrators.name: Ahmad ibn Shu'ayb al-Nasa'i
narrators.note: Compiler of the Sunan, known for the strictest conditions after the two Sahihs.

narrators.name: Muhammad ibn Yazid Ibn Majah
narrators.note: Compiler of the Sunan; graded truthful though the weakest of the six compilers as a narrator.

narrators.name: Muhammad ibn Ishaq
narrators.note: Author of the earliest biography (sirah) of the Prophet; truthful but a mudallis, so his reports are accepted with corroboration.

narrators.name: Abu Hanifa al-Nu'man
narrators.note: Imam of the Hanafi school; foremost as a jurist, and his hadith transmission is debated by rijal critics.

narrators.name: Abdullah ibn Lahi'a
narrators.note: Qadi of Egypt; truthful, but his memory deteriorated after his books were burned, so most critics grade him da'if.

narrators.name: Muhammad ibn Umar al-Waqidi
narrators.note: Celebrated historian, but weak as a hadith narrator; Ahmad and others rejected his isnads.

narrators.name: Jabir ibn Yazid al-Ju'fi
narrators.note: Kufan narrator with Shi'i leanings; graded da'if by most critics and matruk by some.
